candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — immunization and age-appropriate preventive care
candidate.educational_objective: Apply the CDC catch-up immunization principle that extended intervals do not require restarting a properly begun vaccine series.

options.A: Permanently skip delayed vaccine doses because they cannot be given later.
options.B: Use the CDC catch-up schedule; a vaccine series generally does not need to be restarted because of an extended interval between doses.
options.C: Restart every vaccine series from dose 1 whenever the recommended interval has been exceeded.
options.D: Avoid catch-up vaccination because delayed schedules are not recommended for children.

candidate.rationale: CDC's current child and adolescent catch-up schedule states that a vaccine series does not need to be restarted regardless of the time elapsed between doses. The age-appropriate catch-up table and accompanying schedule notes should be used to determine which doses and minimum intervals are needed. Therefore B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For children whose vaccinations have been delayed, vaccine series do not need to be restarted regardless of elapsed time between doses; use the age-appropriate CDC catch-up schedule and notes.
candidate.source_document_title: Catch-up Immunization Schedule for Children and Adolescents
